methodology: One sequential baseline/first-prototype/final startup capture per actual project. Public systemd restart and actual browser GUI, fresh isolated browser contexts, normal motion, installed Chrome, existing project/OS/native metadata caches. No concurrent builds/tests/inference/samplers during startup captures. Same first scene revision/camera and complete final inventory digest; post-inspection comparison checks five full original JSON views. Original raw metadata and source captures remain private, represented here by digests.
limits: First scene/two-rAF and restart-to-observation are presentation/polling proxies, not physical paint or field percentiles. Ready polling additionally follows a screenshot; use the correlated native refresh-job wall interval for complete native observation.

This is earlier map viewing, not faster complete refresh. Saved load/check adds about 1.1–1.4 s; final native complete jobs remain roughly 1.1–1.5 s above this baseline. Directory discovery varies. First uncached preparation is not accelerated.
The initial prototype double-materialized and rewrote unchanged data; final captures and public regression require one materialization, no retention and a new actual directory observation.
Native wall intervals overlap; host thread CPU excludes child workers. Saved metadata is the last successful refresh rather than every subsequent file-detail update or an atomic filesystem snapshot.
Normal input validation and the serial command queue remain; file inspection/model work may still wait for refresh. Large maps use the existing metadata detail cache.

Generic layout, metadata-cache orchestration, observation-revision correspondence, native freshness costs, first-exposure rendering and retirement remain under the original full five-step plan. No new core rule, compiler/parser implementation, generated wire schema, dependency or proof is claimed.
Installed-tool/scripted fixtures are not live-model quality, cold-install, local inference or confidentiality validation.
